1.why: Every MFA endpoint uses access() which loads the account solely from the server-side session userId and rejects client-supplied userId/accountId fields via noId().

2.why: TOTP/recovery verification uses the secret and recovery hashes bound to the session’s own account, so a code does not validate for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets a.mfa/secret on the account and never deletes or invalidates other existing sessions in the sessions Map.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted and recovery codes are stored as salted PBKDF2 hashes, not plaintext.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, and recovery codes are produced with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie is used for secrets, OTPs, or session tokens.

7.why: Server validators email(), phone(), otp(), and recovery() enforce format/length checks on all of those inputs before use.

8.why: UI updates use textContent and JSON APIs, and CSP with nonces is set, so reflected/stored markup is not executed.

9.why: No redirect responses or redirect parameters are honored; noId() rejects a redirect field and the app never issues open redirects.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options DENY on responses.

11.why: Set-Cookie for mfa_session includes HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Stack traces and URL query exposure are avoided, but mock OTPs and recovery codes are written to the on-page logs and console.log.

13.why: Enrollment TOTP is time-windowed and marked provision.used after success; recovery codes are removed on use; provision expires after PROVISION_WINDOW.

14.why: OTP and recovery failures increment counters and lock out for LOCK after MAX attempts via locked()/wrong().

15.why: Sign-in mints a new session id (dropping the prior cookie session), idle/absolute timeouts are enforced, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
